issues.on_page: DISBURSEMENTS AND TRANSFERS: General Government 1,419,009; Public Safety 382,548; Public Works 764,387; Public Health and Social Services 129,436; Culture and Recreation 532,828; Community Development 1,626,512
issues.issue: [fixed] These lines include transfers and other financing uses. 4,854,720 - statement expenditures 2,784,735 (p10) = 2,069,985, which is exactly gross governmental transfers out 1,294,735 (584,002 + 116,615 + 26,296 + 4,660 + 297,941 + 265,221, pp11-12) + Sales Tax Loan Advances 769,250 + Purchase of Assets for Resale 6,000. Gross transfers in (1,374,195) are already recorded as other financing (detail[10]), so the transfers end up counted as spending. Per the hidden-transfer rule, add a negative contra line per affected group (split_from naming p21 and pp11-12, review) plus the matching other-financing lines. detail_totals[1] (10,696,715) should then carry includes ['other financing'].

[fixed] Broad group whose make-up can be traced: business-type operating revenues alone are 5,313,719 (p15: charges for services 4,295,851, NPPD 473,237, merchandise 469,425...), well over half the line. The rule says to use the dominant category, charges for services/fees (detail 'other charges for services' or electric charges), with review naming the mix, not 'other'.

issues.on_page: Local Receipts: Other 6,693,542 (Total Primary Government schedule)
issues.issue: Most of this line is business-type (utility and golf receipts), but it is tagged governmental. The revenue lines on this all-funds schedule mix both fund types.
Equals Homestead 48,051 + Property Tax Credit 61,321 + State Highway Maintenance 13,194 (p8). That is 89% homestead/tax credits, so detail_category 'homestead/tax credits' with review fits better.
